Custom Pizza Boxes: Printing and Grease Resistance for Takeaway Brands

Published August 21, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

Specify pizza boxes by internal size, board grade, grease-resistance level, venting and print. For hot greasy pizza, confirm the barrier and printing suitability with the actual product. Check stacking strength for delivery stacks and confirm food-contact documents for your market before mass production.

Decision table

RequirementTypical choiceBuyer check
BoardE-flute or paperboard by sizeStack and fold strength
Grease barrierAqueous coating or PE-coatedTest with hot pizza
VentingSteam vents in lidPrevents soggy crust
PrintFlexo or offset, 1–4 colorsFood-safe inks

Size the box to the pizza

Measure the pizza diameter and depth including toppings. A box that is too small crushes the pizza; one that is too large lets it slide. Confirm the internal clearance and how the lid closes without touching the food.

Barrier decisions affect cost and claims

Aqueous grease-resistant coatings handle typical takeaway use and keep the box recyclable in many programs. PE coatings give stronger barrier but change recyclability claims. Test the exact pizza, temperature and delivery time before choosing, and confirm coating documentation for your market.

Printing and brand experience

Pizza boxes travel to the customer and often appear in delivery photos. Full-color inside printing, branded lids and clean die lines build recognition. Confirm ink suitability for food contact and that print does not reduce barrier performance.

Stacking and delivery reality

Delivery riders stack boxes. Check lid lock strength, board stiffness and how heat and grease affect the stack after 20–40 minutes. Request a packed test with real pizzas before approving bulk production.

Buyer checklist

  1. Confirm pizza diameter and depth
  2. Select barrier by delivery time
  3. Add venting and test steam behavior
  4. Verify print and ink suitability
  5. Test stacked hot delivery

Frequently asked questions

Do pizza boxes need special paper?

Corrugated or paperboard with a grease barrier is typical; confirm the combination with the actual hot product.

Can pizza boxes be fully printed inside?

Yes, inside printing is common, but confirm food-safe inks and that print does not affect the barrier.

How do I know the barrier works?

Test with hot pizza at the expected delivery time and inspect for oil soak-through and sogginess.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Pizza boxes are a paperboard and coating job. Kraft or white cardboard at 250–400 gsm with food-safe, grease-resistant coatings is standard; E-flute corrugated adds stacking strength for delivery. Printing is offset, flexo or digital at 1–8 colors with CMYK + Pantone matching. The vent pattern and locking tabs are confirmed from your box dimensions on the free dieline. MOQ is 500 PCS per size and artwork, sampling 5–7 working days after artwork confirmation, production 2–4 weeks.

Frequently Asked Questions

How is grease resistance achieved?

Food-safe coatings are applied to the board; the specific coating is confirmed with the approved structure.

Can pizza boxes be full-color printed?

Yes — offset, flexo or digital printing at 1–8 colors with CMYK + Pantone matching.
